full_judgment:
A.K.M. Asaduzzaman, J. This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the accused petitioner should not be enlarged on bail in Criminal Misc. Case No. 9166 of 2010 arising out of Khilgaon P.S. Case No.34 dated 16.4.2010 under section 364/34 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 At present her husband is a Garments businessman. On 11.9.2010 at about 4.00 P.M. he left the house and went to Mohakhali Hotel for urgent meeting. On the same date at 7.52 minute her husband on mobile informed her that he was at Fakirapul. It will be late to come of residence. Next she got his mobile stop. On 12.4.10 at about 7.30 A.M. an unknown man mobile her to say that your husband is in our custody. He will not come at all to your residence. If you give Tk.50,00000/- then your husband will return to you. Next to stop his mobile. On 12.4.2010 at 1.50 P.M. her husband asked her to arrange Tk. 50,00000/- to save him from their custody. On 15.4.10 at 3.32 minute an unknown man mobile came to her and asked her how much money do you arrange ? Then she informed that she has arranged Tk.3/4 lacs only. Then the unknown man asked her that it is not sufficient. Thereafter to look into her husband, she knows that her husband was detained to the A.G.B Colony Club of one shown. Her conception is that due to business dispute, previous enmity, and money transaction her husband’s friend accused (1) Md. Abdul Hannan (2) Md. A. Hakim Bepari (3) Abdullah (4) Sawon (5) Nazmul (6) Emon and others on 11.4.2010 at about 4.00 p.m, the accuseds called her husband from her residence for the purpose of killing by kidnapping detained him an unknown place, hence the case. 

 On perusal of the confessional statement as well as considering the factual aspect of the case to the effect that even after expiry of the statutory period of limitation the police could not conclude the investigation, we find substance in the submission of the learned advocate for the petitioner and also considering that the petitioner has got fair chance of acquittal in this case and as such we are inclined to enlarge him on bail. We find merits in this rule. 

 In the result, the rule is made absolute. The petitioner Md. Abdul Hakim Bepari, son of late Salaman Bepari may find bail on furnishing bail bond subject to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Criminal Misc. Case No. 9166 of 2010 arising out of Khilgaon P.S. Case No.34 dated 16.4.2010. The trial court however, is at liberty to cancel the bail, if the accused petitioner misuses in any way the privilege of bail.
